title: Terminal and Colony Again
premise: Juniper Marchetti smuggles memories along a silent trade corridor between two warring colonies, keeping her head down and her ledger clean. When a ghost ship's manifest lists her dead brother's name, she discovers the fleet manufactured the war's inciting incident — and hid the proof in a memory canister she unknowingly carried for years. Hunted by fleet intelligence and the smugglers' syndicate alike, Juniper must choose between the lover she left on the other side of the blockade and the truth that could free them both. She delivers the memory to a joint tribunal at the eleventh hour, exposing the conspiracy and shattering the truce into a fragile, hard-won peace — at the cost of her brother's posthumous innocence and her own immunity.
about_author: Coral Dunmore is a former maritime radio operator who turned to science fiction after a decade of listening to voices crossing oceans that didn't want to hear each other. She writes from a converted lighthouse keeper's cottage, where she claims the fog does half the editing.

chapters.title: The Long Quiet Route
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. She runs a memory canister past orbital customs on the freighter Vesperine, using a customs officer's boredom and her own flawless false identity. We learn her rules: never open the cargo, never take sides, never return to Calloway Station. The beat is competent solitude — a woman who has made invisibility an art form, and likes it that way.

chapters.title: A Name on a Manifest
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Docking at neutral Halloway Ring, she audits her own ledger and finds an impossible entry: the ship Aldrin-9 — scrapped before the war — listed her brother Tomas as crew on a voyage that never flew. The emotional beat is a cold spike of dread; her carefully sealed past has a crack in it, and something is leaking through.

chapters.title: The Man Who Buys Silence
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. A fleet intelligence officer, Commander Reyes, approaches her with a polite offer: surrender any Aldrin-9 cargo and walk away rich. She lies beautifully. The beat is a cat-and-mouse conversation where both know the other is lying, establishing Reyes as charming, patient, and genuinely dangerous.

chapters.title: What the Canister Remembers
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV, breaking her first rule. She plays the canister she carried for years and experiences a recorded memory: a fleet officer ordering the strike on the Calloway grain convoy — the incident that started the war — and a young voice objecting: Tomas. The beat is grief detonating into fury.

chapters.title: Calloway, Still Burning
chapters.summary: POV shifts to Idris Vale, Juniper's former lover and now a Calloway tribunal archivist. He catalogs war-crimes testimony that never gets read. A smuggled message reaches him: a single phrase only Juniper would know. The beat is longing braided with duty — he wants her back and knows wanting her is a security breach.

chapters.title: The Syndicate's Cut
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. The Meridian syndicate that employed her reveals it has known about the canister all along and plans to sell the truth back to the fleet — burying it. Her handler Sef offers her a share and a warning: run, and every port closes to her. The beat is betrayal; her neutral world was never neutral, just bought.

chapters.title: Ghost Ship, Real Wreck
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. She tracks Aldrin-9's last flight path to a debris field and boards the hulk, finding evidence the ship was scuttled to fake its decommission — and a second canister slot, empty. Someone else took a copy. The beat is claustrophobic dread that resolves into resolve: she's not chasing a memory anymore, she's chasing a witness.

chapters.title: Reyes at the Airlock
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Reyes catches her at the wreck, but instead of arresting her, he confesses: he's been ordered to retrieve and destroy the memory, and he's tired of being the fleet's hands. He gives her a window — forty hours before the truce expires — and lets her go. The beat is uneasy alliance; the hunter becomes a reluctant ally with a countdown attached.

chapters.title: Forty Hours
chapters.summary: Idris's POV. On Calloway, the tribunal is about to ratify a peace that codifies the official lie. Idris finds an anomaly in the convoy records that matches the phrase in Juniper's message. He must decide whether to trust a smuggler's ghost or the institution that raised him. The beat is loyalty cracking against truth.

chapters.title: The Blockade Run
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. She threads the Calloway blockade in the Vesperine with Reyes aboard as insurance, dodging patrol nets and a syndicate bounty ship. The sequence is pure velocity — near-misses, a silent running pass through a debris corridor. The beat is terror transmuted into exhilaration: for the first time in years she's flying toward something.

chapters.title: What We Buried at Calloway
chapters.summary: Juniper and Idris's shared scene, alternating close POV. Reunion in a tribunal archive basement — ten seconds of almost-touching before the argument: he wants to go through channels; she knows the channels are the conspiracy. The beat is love against duty made literal, both of them right, both of them terrified.

chapters.title: The Witness Nobody Wanted
chapters.summary: Idris's POV. They locate the second canister's carrier: a disgraced fleet medic, Ada Okonkwo, living under a dead name in Calloway's undercity. Ada confirms the recording is authentic but refuses to testify — the last time she tried, her family was killed. The beat is the cost of truth, told by someone already paying it.

chapters.title: Sef's Ledger
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. The syndicate closes in; Sef offers a final deal — the canister for her life and Idris's. She stalls, and we learn Sef's motive: his own daughter died in the convoy strike, and he believes selling the secret back is the only way to keep anyone else from dying for it. The beat is a villain with a wound, and Juniper almost believing him.

chapters.title: Truce Expiry
chapters.summary: Multiple POV. The ceasefire lapses; fleet squadrons and Calloway militia move to forward positions. Reyes transmits a warning he shouldn't: the fleet plans to strike the tribunal itself and blame Calloway. The beat is the world tilting — the deadline isn't a deadline anymore, it's a fuse.

chapters.title: The Tribunal Basement
chapters.summary: Idris's POV. Ada agrees to testify if Idris guarantees her anonymity through the archive's sealed-witness protocol — a protocol the tribunal president has been quietly disabling. Idris must forge his own institution's records to protect her. The beat is justice outside the law, committed by a man who believed in the law.

chapters.title: Everything Juniper Owes
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. She surrenders herself to Sef as a decoy so the canister can reach the tribunal, expecting a cell and finding instead Sef's private grief — he plays his daughter's last memory for her. She tells him the truth isn't a commodity; it's the only thing that can't be bought back. The beat is persuasion as climax-in-miniature, and Sef's silence as a door left open.

chapters.title: The Strike Order
chapters.summary: Reyes's POV. Ordered to lead the strike on the tribunal, Reyes instead broadcasts the fleet's own strike order on open channels — mutiny as testimony. He is arrested mid-transmission, smiling. The beat is a soldier choosing the law over the legal, buying Juniper the hours she needs with his career and probably his life.

chapters.title: Deliver the Message
chapters.summary: Juniper and Idris, alternating POV. The final run: through a tribunal building under evacuation, canister in hand, syndicate and fleet security both closing in — until Sef's people, unprompted, hold the corridor. Juniper plugs the memory into the open session. The beat is the climax: the war's founding lie playing in front of both delegations at once.

chapters.title: The Recording
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV. The tribunal watches the convoy strike — and Tomas's voice objecting, then dying. Calloway and fleet delegates react in real time; the president's cover-up unravels on the record. Ada testifies under sealed witness. The beat is catharsis without comfort: truth lands, and everyone in the room is smaller for it.

chapters.title: After the Verdict
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. The tribunal voids the war's legal basis; a real ceasefire is signed. Reyes faces a tribunal of his own, and Juniper testifies for him. Sef walks free on technicalities and doesn't look at her. The beat is the hollow morning after victory — justice done, and no one feels clean.

chapters.title: Tomas's Name, Cleared
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. She formally petitions to restore her brother's record and learns the full story of his last flight: he stole the second canister to protect the witness, and died getting it off the ship. Grief finally has a shape she can hold. The beat is mourning that resolves into inheritance — she finishes what he started.

chapters.title: The Route Between Worlds That Speak
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV, final chapter. With the corridor reopening, she takes one last contract — legal, boring, beautiful — carrying ordinary memories between worlds that are talking again. Idris is aboard, off-duty, off-duty of everything. She opens a canister at last: her own, a recording of Tomas laughing, kept not smuggled. The beat is peace earned, not granted.
